headline: Regulatory network inference shifts toward perturbation, temporal and circadian structure
label: Dynamic Regulatory Network Inference
summary: New preprints and papers tie GRN inference to perturbation paths, temporal embeddings and circadian data, with a simulator and database supporting benchmarking.
synthesis: The common thread is inferring regulatory network structure from time-resolved or perturbation-derived data, rather than from static co-variation. GSET selects compact gene sets from temporal embedding trajectories using optimal transport residuals and KL divergence to inform mechanistic GRN inference. REGA-perturb resolves perturbation effects through TF-regulatory element-gene paths using reference epigenomes and Perturb-seq latent programs, while CausalODE learns causal graphs via a causal reach metric on latent mediator dynamics. MAGE addresses age-indexed gene sets in time-varying networks. scCircaSim and CircaVal supply circadian simulation with known phases and rhythm parameters, and multi-omics resources across species. The items differ in modality and maturity, and the earlier microbial association framing is not supported by these items.
